prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick one single “best” roofer for Denver without checking current local listings and reviews, but I can help you find the right contractor and avoid common hail‑repair scams. Two quick questions so I can help more precisely:
- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver are you in?
- Do you already have an insurance claim open?

If you want to start now, here’s a practical checklist and plan to find the best roofer for hail damage:

What to require from any roofer
- License & insurance: Verify they carry general liability and workers’ comp and ask for their registration/contractor number. Confirm a local business address and phone.  
- Manufacturer certification: For shingle warranties, ask whether they are a certified installer for the shingle brand they’ll use.  
- Written, itemized estimate: Materials, labor, disposal, permit fees, and timeline. Look for estimates based on a roof inspection (not just satellite).  
- Warranty: Ask about both workmanship warranty (company) and manufacturer shingle warranty. Get warranties in writing.  
- Permits & inspections: They should pull local permits and schedule inspections if required.  
- Insurance claim experience: If you’re filing through homeowners insurance, a roofer experienced with claims and Xactimate estimates is helpful.  
- References & portfolio: Ask for local references and recent photos of completed hail repairs. Check Google/Bing, BBB, Yelp, and Nextdoor for recent reviews.

Red flags / things to avoid
- High-pressure sales, “storm chasers” who show up unsolicited after a storm.  
- Large upfront payment (avoid full payment before work starts; a typical schedule is small deposit, balance as work completes).  
- Cash-only offers or no written contract.  
- No physical address or no verifiable local crew.

How to compare bids
- Get at least 3 written estimates.  
- Ensure each bid uses the same scope (e.g., full roof replacement vs. spot repairs, same shingle brand/type).  
- Compare warranty terms, removal of old shingles, and whether they will reinstall/replace flashing, vents, gutters as needed.  
- Ask about timeline and the crew performing the work (subcontractors vs. company employees).

Where to verify credentials and reviews
- Google Business reviews, Yelp, Nextdoor.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB).  
- Manufacturer locator pages (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) to find certified contractors.  
- Colorado contractor registration/consumer protection pages (verify local requirements).

Insurance claim tips
- Take photos of damage and date-stamp them.  
- Get your own inspection and independent estimate if you’re unsure the adjuster’s assessment is complete.  
- Don’t sign over your insurance check to the contractor; get a contractor lien waiver when final payment is made.  
- If the insurer undervalues the damage, a reputable roofer can provide a detailed estimate to support your claim.

If you want, I can:
- Help draft an email/text to send to contractors asking the right questions.  
- Create a short comparison checklist to score bids.  
- Look up and shortlist well‑rated local roofers if you tell me your ZIP code (I’ll need your location because I can’t browse the web for you).

Which would you prefer?
